page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.large is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine instance within the ecs.c1 server family. It is provisioned with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor.
This instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data. It features zero GPUs and does not bundle complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The underlying CPU architecture lacks advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-assisted cryptography (AES, SHA-NI). This absence of vector and matrix acceleration limits its efficiency for modern machine learning, heavy cryptography, and complex mathematical simulations.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c1.large is structured for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Suitable workloads include standard web serving, batch processing, and legacy compute tasks that do not rely on modern vector instruction sets.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c1.large is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance within the ecs.c1 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating external network-attached storage for data persistence. Hardware analysis indicates a lack of modern CPU instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptography. Consequently, the instance is best suited for legacy compute tasks, basic web serving, and lightweight batch processing workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but do not rely on specialized vector or matrix instructions.
